                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Cancerous cells with decreased MHC class I expression are less recognizable by cytotoxic T-cells, which rely on MHC class I for antigen presentation. This reduction in MHC class I allows these tumor cells to evade detection by the adaptive immune response. However, natural killer (NK) cells can recognize and kill these tumor cells due to their ability to detect stress signals and the absence of MHC class I. Therefore, NK cells are the most capable immune cells of targeting and eliminating these cancerous cells. This reasoning aligns with the consensus that NK cells play a crucial role in recognizing and destroying cells with reduced MHC class I expression.
